rationale: All runs are limited by a port path and setup repair never engages (slack >= +5 ns). Inferring a 20%-of-target I/O delay, T_eff ~ 0.2*target + d_io: d_io is ~3.85 ns with timing-driven placement and orfs/stock wires (bm64, aes, r1-1, regardless of synthesis or slew margin), ~4.25 with cap213 (likely slower clock tree/extra buffering) and 5.2-6.0 without TD; reg-to-reg needs only 4.2-5.6 ns. So keep period_frac 0.45 and the r1-1 recipe, and test single placement levers on d_io: (1) maximum density (+30) to contract the timing-weighted port nets and clock tree; (2) utilisation 30 for a smaller die with shorter pin-to-flop and clock wires.
